# Statement ledger

This ledger maps labels of the manuscript on the second moment of the
Stratonovich hyperbolic Anderson model with Gaussian noise fractional in time
to the Lean declarations in this package. Labels and TeX line numbers refer to
the manuscript revision a284420, and labels are written exactly as in its
LaTeX source (for example `P:clock-copy-obstruction`). The ledger was written
and reviewed at the earlier revisions cf979d6, 669ccc9, ba01d98, 3920258 and
975feb3. Revision a284420 makes two mathematical edits that the ledger
follows. (1) In `notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex` it adds Lemma
`L:spatial-fourier-bound` (lines 101-164, display `E:spatial-fourier-bound`),
the deterministic bound `A_sp(g) <= 2^(1+alpha) R_alpha b^(alpha/2)` that
`SpatialFourierBound` already proved, and the proof of
`P:spatial-smooth-ratio` (same label and statement) now derives `R_0 < inf`
from it, independently of the finiteness of `S_1^pos`, which it keeps only
for the score inequality. (2) In the main file, `L:damped-homogeneous-norms`
replaces its smoothing and truncation sentence by the multiplier comparison
`E:damped-multiplier-comparison` (a measurable multiplier `m` in `[0,1]`,
nested measurable Laplace domains, positivity after time integration,
scaling asserted only for the original covariance) and its proof by the
corresponding argument. The other changes since 975feb3 are prose and front
matter (title, abstract, preface, a theory-outlook chapter, the reader
edition, Appendices F and G, the list of notation moved to the back).
Every cited label exists exactly once at a284420. Three of them are new at
a284420 and do not exist at 975feb3: `L:spatial-fourier-bound`,
`E:spatial-fourier-bound` and `E:damped-multiplier-comparison`. Every other
cited label exists exactly once, in the same file, at both revisions, and
every such cited lemma, proposition, theorem, equation and section has the
same statement and proof up to whitespace and braces, except
`P:spatial-smooth-ratio` (proof only), `L:damped-homogeneous-norms`
(statement and proof) and the section `S:spatial-occupation-foundation`
(the new lemma). TeX line numbers were moved to a284420 by a line map; each
moved range has the same text at both revisions, and the ranges inside the
two edited passages were mapped to the corresponding new passages by hand
(script checks recorded in `provenance/manuscript-anchor.json`).

## Scope

- The "What it states" column is a faithful paraphrase, sometimes
  shortened. The exact statement is the Lean type in
  `StratonovichHAMAudit/<Module>.lean` (step modules) or
  `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/<Module>.lean` (library modules: whole results, narrower results, foundations and proof steps);
  `Audit/<module>/` prints the elaborated types.
- The rows cover every public theorem (2050) and 418 definitions whose
  values are stated as facts or that name a manuscript object. The other 89
  public definitions have no rows of their own: 85 (for example `kappa`,
  `delta`, `gauge`, `counts`, `InventoryProduct.partialEval`,
  `OccupationPhysicalClass.volI`, `SpaceTimePositivity.timeMeasure`,
  `TerminalWick.chainMassReal`, `WaveGreenFourier.spherePhi` and
  `OccupationCeilingExact.stepG`) only name quantities or measures used in
  those statements, and four are the instances that make
  `TimeCompletion.Pre` a pre-inner-product space; read their bodies in the
  Lean source or in `Audit/`.
- The `StratonovichHAMAudit` modules check finite, algebraic and scalar
  steps only: exact identities, polynomial and rational certificates,
  real-power bookkeeping, parameter ranges, and a few finite-dimensional
  inner-product and finite-word facts. The exception is `HermiteWordFock`
  (wave L9), which applies `HermiteWord.cut_eq_raw` to the Fock model of
  `FockForm` and so formalizes the special case of `L:finite-word-cutoff`
  with one Gaussian coordinate per color (section "HermiteWordFock (narrower result: `L:finite-word-cutoff` for one Gaussian mode per color and single finite words; finite sums and Bochner integrals not formalized)"); the
  multi-mode case is not formalized.
- Section headings use three categories. (A) "whole result": every
  conclusion of the labelled result is a Lean conclusion under the
  manuscript's hypotheses, possibly with named supplied inputs that are
  disclosed (coverage class same-assumptions or inputs-supplied, conclusion
  full); no other section carries it. (B) "narrower result: ...": a labelled
  result some of whose conclusions are not Lean conclusions, or are proved
  for a modelled object (the class `O` by joint representatives, the rate in
  Rayleigh form, the cost in integral form, an abstract structure standing
  for an object the manuscript constructs, an object that is not constructed)
  whose identification with the manuscript's object is not formalized; the
  heading names what is missing. The one exception is a registered model
  choice (next item): a result whose only modelled object is such a choice
  stays a whole result, and its section names the model.
  Discharging a named input in a completion module does not turn a narrower
  result into a whole one. (C) "foundation: ..." or "proof steps ...": facts
  used by labelled results, not a labelled result themselves; every
  `StratonovichHAMAudit` section except `HermiteWordFock` is of this kind.
  The first cell of an Index row uses the same words.
- Model-choice register. A registered model choice is a documented
  definitional choice that is the standard construction of a manuscript
  object, recorded with the identification that is not formalized. M1 (wave
  L6, Le's decision 4): the wave Green measure in `d = 3` is
  `(s/(4 pi)) map (omega -> s omega) volume.toSphere`, Mathlib's sphere
  measure scaled to the radius-`s` sphere; its identification with the
  surface (Hausdorff or Riemannian) measure of the TeX is not proved. Results
  whose only modelled object is M1 (`L:low-alpha-convolution`,
  `L:phase-contractions`, and the sections `LowAlphaConvolution`,
  `PhaseContractions` and `L9Completed`) are whole results. Missing
  constructions are not model choices: they make a result narrower (for

  solution moments of `P:moment-growth-logconvex` and
  `C:static-moment-constant-continuity`).

# Formalization scope

## The paper's argument and where Lean enters

The paper bounds and identifies the growth of `log E[u(t,x)²]` for the
Stratonovich hyperbolic Anderson model. The argument has three layers.

1. **Stochastic and analytic layer.** The chaos expansion, the two-chain
   pairing integrals, Wick pairings (beyond finite families of Gaussian
   values), Gaussian integration (beyond finitely many standard Gaussians),
   imported bounds,
   Laplace transforms and the variational asymptotics. **Not in Lean**,
   except a few slices: the Laplace transforms of the wave kernel and of
   the two-time kernel and the subordination formula (`ClockCopy` and its
   foundation modules), the Gaussian transform of the spectral measure
   (`MaskedSpectralGrowth`), the uniform scalar frequency row
   (`FrequencyRow`), the temporal completion `H_a` (`TimeCompletion`), the
   auxiliary mask norm (`MaskedAuxiliaryNorm`), the Gaussian heat envelope
   of the covariance (`VariationalMean`), a finite Hilbert-valued Bessel
   inequality (`PhaseBessel`), the wave Green measures `G_s` for
   `d = 1, 2, 3` (`WaveGreen`), the spectral identity and positive
   definiteness of `Gamma = delta_0(dx_1) dx_2` (`QuotientObstruction`), a
   finite Gaussian comparison under the positive semidefinite order
   (`GaussianComparison`), the two wave variance directions in spectral
   form (`WaveTwoVariances`), the variational floor and the Rayleigh-form
   rate (`VariationalFloor`, `VariationalRate`), the deterministic Fourier
   bound `L:spatial-fourier-bound` for the smooth spatial ratio and the
   static controls
   (`SpatialFourierBound`, `SpatialSmoothRatio`, `SpatialStaticControls`,
   `SpatialOccupationCompleted`), series types and the continuity of the
   growth types in the temporal exponent (`SeriesType`, `TypeContinuity`),
   the white-noise bound formulas and clock transforms
   (`WhiteRelativeWidth`, `WhiteClockLaplace`), the coefficient bound of
   the interval inventory product (`InventoryProduct`), an abstract `L^2`
   limit of a regularized series under a uniform scaled moment bound
   (`UniformSeriesTail`), the density of test functions in the
   weak-gradient `H^1` (`H1Density`), the physical four-linear extension
   and the spatial energy (`SpatialFourLinear`), the full physical
   occupation class (`OccupationPhysicalClass`; both completed in
   `SpatialOccupationL7Completed`), the scalar and Hilbert-space steps
   of the static interaction and interval coefficient bounds
   (`IntervalScalar`, `IntervalScalarCompleted`), the spectral-mass
   identity `R_Gamma(1) = R_alpha` (`SpectralMassIdentity`), Gaussian
   smoothing as a Fourier multiplier (`DampedMultiplier`), the positivity of
   the space-time occupation form, the deterministic occupation ceiling and
   the spatial bracket (`SpaceTimePositivity`, `OccupationCeilingFinite`,
   `SpatialBracket`, completed in `L8Completed`), the masked rates
   (`RemoveMask`), the finite Wick formula and the terminal-chain Wick
   formula with the chain measures given by their masses (`FiniteWick`,
   `TerminalWick`), an abstract compact Young baseline (`SymplecticFree`)
   and the Cauchy steps of the static phase orders (`StaticPhaseCauchy`),
   the Fourier transforms of the wave Green measures in `d = 1, 2, 3` and
   Archimedes' law for the sphere measure (`WaveGreenFourier`), the low-alpha
   convolution bound and the static contraction bounds
   (`LowAlphaConvolution`, `PhaseContractions`, completed in `L9Completed`),
   the exact occupation constant and ceiling (`RawOccupationEnergy`,
   `OccupationCeilingExact`), the normalized Hermite polynomials and the
   finite Gaussian Fock layer with values in a Hilbert factor
   (`GaussianHermite`, `HermiteFock`) and their consumers `L:fock-form`,
   `L:interval-contractions` and `E:occupied-multiplication` (`FockForm`),
   and the scalar and numerical-range steps of the complex phase bounds
   (`ComplexPhaseScalar`).
2. **Reductions to explicit inequalities.** At many points the analytic
   argument reduces to a finite statement: an exponent range, an exact
   rational or square-root inequality, a polynomial that must stay positive
   on a region, a determinant or matrix inverse, a count of coefficients in
   a finite word, or an integral comparison once integrability is known.
   **These are what Lean checks.**
3. **Assembly** of the main theorems from the layers above. **Not in Lean.**

So each module checks one reduction in layer 2. Its hypotheses state the
facts that layer 1 supplies (for example positivity of a parameter,
integrability of a function, or an inequality proved analytically in the
paper). Its conclusion is the fact that the paper then uses.

`TimeFractional`, `WaveKernel`, `GaussianIBP`, `GaussianTest` and

These counts describe the package. They are not a percentage of the paper.
The 25 whole results and 18 narrower results with the manuscript's

## Reading a statement

For each declaration, check three things against the paper:

1. the hypotheses match what the paper has available at that point;
2. the conclusion is what the paper uses next;
3. parameter ranges, strict versus non-strict inequalities and quantifier
   order agree.

The [statement ledger](docs/statement-ledger.md) records this for every row.
`Audit/<module>/` prints the full elaborated types, so the statements can be
read without opening an editor.

## Not yet included

Three development modules use a Gaussian-chaos library that is not yet
public: normalized Gaussian coordinates, vector Gaussian projection and
colored vector words. They are checked in the private development record
and will be added here when that library is released.

## Possible next steps

- the finite pair-partition counts behind the two-chain integrals;
- a reusable Laplace-to-time growth lemma, with its analytic inputs as
  hypotheses;
- the constant and exponent algebra of the main upper and lower bounds.

     2	
     3	## The paper's argument and where Lean enters
     4	
     5	The paper bounds and identifies the growth of `log E[u(t,x)²]` for the
     6	Stratonovich hyperbolic Anderson model. The argument has three layers.
     7	
     8	1. **Stochastic and analytic layer.** The chaos expansion, the two-chain
     9	   pairing integrals, Wick pairings (beyond finite families of Gaussian
    10	   values), Gaussian integration (beyond finitely many standard Gaussians),
    11	   imported bounds,
    12	   Laplace transforms and the variational asymptotics. **Not in Lean**,
    13	   except a few slices: the Laplace transforms of the wave kernel and of
    14	   the two-time kernel and the subordination formula (`ClockCopy` and its
    15	   foundation modules), the Gaussian transform of the spectral measure
    16	   (`MaskedSpectralGrowth`), the uniform scalar frequency row
    17	   (`FrequencyRow`), the temporal completion `H_a` (`TimeCompletion`), the
    18	   auxiliary mask norm (`MaskedAuxiliaryNorm`), the Gaussian heat envelope
    19	   of the covariance (`VariationalMean`), a finite Hilbert-valued Bessel
    20	   inequality (`PhaseBessel`), the wave Green measures `G_s` for
    21	   `d = 1, 2, 3` (`WaveGreen`), the spectral identity and positive
    22	   definiteness of `Gamma = delta_0(dx_1) dx_2` (`QuotientObstruction`), a
    23	   finite Gaussian comparison under the positive semidefinite order
    24	   (`GaussianComparison`), the two wave variance directions in spectral
    25	   form (`WaveTwoVariances`), the variational floor and the Rayleigh-form
    26	   rate (`VariationalFloor`, `VariationalRate`), the deterministic Fourier
    27	   bound `L:spatial-fourier-bound` for the smooth spatial ratio and the
    28	   static controls
    29	   (`SpatialFourierBound`, `SpatialSmoothRatio`, `SpatialStaticControls`,
    30	   `SpatialOccupationCompleted`), series types and the continuity of the
    31	   growth types in the temporal exponent (`SeriesType`, `TypeContinuity`),
    32	   the white-noise bound formulas and clock transforms
    33	   (`WhiteRelativeWidth`, `WhiteClockLaplace`), the coefficient bound of
    34	   the interval inventory product (`InventoryProduct`), an abstract `L^2`
    35	   limit of a regularized series under a uniform scaled moment bound
    36	   (`UniformSeriesTail`), the density of test functions in the
    37	   weak-gradient `H^1` (`H1Density`), the physical four-linear extension
    38	   and the spatial energy (`SpatialFourLinear`), the full physical
    39	   occupation class (`OccupationPhysicalClass`; both completed in
    40	   `SpatialOccupationL7Completed`), the scalar and Hilbert-space steps
    41	   of the static interaction and interval coefficient bounds
    42	   (`IntervalScalar`, `IntervalScalarCompleted`), the spectral-mass
    43	   identity `R_Gamma(1) = R_alpha` (`SpectralMassIdentity`), Gaussian
    44	   smoothing as a Fourier multiplier (`DampedMultiplier`), the positivity of
    45	   the space-time occupation form, the deterministic occupation ceiling and
    46	   the spatial bracket (`SpaceTimePositivity`, `OccupationCeilingFinite`,
    47	   `SpatialBracket`, completed in `L8Completed`), the masked rates
    48	   (`RemoveMask`), the finite Wick formula and the terminal-chain Wick
    49	   formula with the chain measures given by their masses (`FiniteWick`,
    50	   `TerminalWick`), an abstract compact Young baseline (`SymplecticFree`)
    51	   and the Cauchy steps of the static phase orders (`StaticPhaseCauchy`),
    52	   the Fourier transforms of the wave Green measures in `d = 1, 2, 3` and
    53	   Archimedes' law for the sphere measure (`WaveGreenFourier`), the low-alpha
    54	   convolution bound and the static contraction bounds
    55	   (`LowAlphaConvolution`, `PhaseContractions`, completed in `L9Completed`),
    56	   the exact occupation constant and ceiling (`RawOccupationEnergy`,
    57	   `OccupationCeilingExact`), the normalized Hermite polynomials and the
    58	   finite Gaussian Fock layer with values in a Hilbert factor
    59	   (`GaussianHermite`, `HermiteFock`) and their consumers `L:fock-form`,
    60	   `L:interval-contractions` and `E:occupied-multiplication` (`FockForm`),
    61	   and the scalar and numerical-range steps of the complex phase bounds
    62	   (`ComplexPhaseScalar`).
    63	2. **Reductions to explicit inequalities.** At many points the analytic
    64	   argument reduces to a finite statement: an exponent range, an exact
    65	   rational or square-root inequality, a polynomial that must stay positive
    66	   on a region, a determinant or matrix inverse, a count of coefficients in
    67	   a finite word, or an integral comparison once integrability is known.
    68	   **These are what Lean checks.**
    69	3. **Assembly** of the main theorems from the layers above. **Not in Lean.**
    70	
    71	So each module checks one reduction in layer 2. Its hypotheses state the
    72	facts that layer 1 supplies (for example positivity of a parameter,
    73	integrability of a function, or an inequality proved analytically in the
    74	paper). Its conclusion is the fact that the paper then uses.

   135	## Reading a statement
   136	
   137	For each declaration, check three things against the paper:
   138	
   139	1. the hypotheses match what the paper has available at that point;
   140	2. the conclusion is what the paper uses next;
   141	3. parameter ranges, strict versus non-strict inequalities and quantifier
   142	   order agree.
   143	
   144	The [statement ledger](docs/statement-ledger.md) records this for every row.
   145	`Audit/<module>/` prints the full elaborated types, so the statements can be
   146	read without opening an editor.
   147	
   148	## Not yet included
   149	
   150	Three development modules use a Gaussian-chaos library that is not yet
   151	public: normalized Gaussian coordinates, vector Gaussian projection and
   152	colored vector words. They are checked in the private development record
   153	and will be added here when that library is released.

1	\section{Covariance bounds for physically masked wave fields}
     2	\label{S:masked-covariance}
     3	
     4	We establish the covariance estimates needed for the operator construction.
     5	Throughout this section, Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog} holds, $a = \alpha_0$, and
     6	$\Gamma \ne 0$. For zero spatial covariance, the spatial spectral measures and
     7	noise variances vanish; the purely temporal estimates remain valid independently
     8	of $\Gamma$. We use the unitary Fourier transform
     9	\[
    10	  \widehat{f}(\xi) = c_d\int_{\R^d}e^{-i\xi\cdot x}f(x)\ud x,
    11	  \qquad c_d = (2\pi)^{-d/2}.
    12	\]
    13	The spectral convention in Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog} means that, for every
    14	complex Schwartz test $\varphi$,
    15	\begin{equation}\label{E:masked-spectral-convention}
    16	  \int_{\R^d}\varphi(x)\Gamma(\ud x)
    17	  = \int_{\R^d}\left(\int_{\R^d}e^{i\xi\cdot x}
    18	  \varphi(x)\ud x\right)\mu(\ud\xi).
    19	\end{equation}
    20	This is an identity of distribution pairings. We will not interchange two
    21	infinite measures in the associated oscillatory expression.
    22	
    23	A positive tempered Radon measure has polynomial mass growth. Indeed, choose a
    24	nonnegative compact smooth test that is at least one on the unit ball, and apply
    25	a defining Schwartz seminorm bound for the distribution to its dilations. Its
    26	mass on a ball of radius $R \ge 1$ is bounded by a power of $R$. Summation over
    27	dyadic shells then gives integrability of $(1+|x|)^{-N}$ for some $N$, and hence
    28	absolute integrability of every Schwartz test. These facts apply to both
    29	$\Gamma$ and $\mu$. Smooth cutoffs converge in the Schwartz topology, so these
    30	integrals agree with the tempered pairings.
    31	
    32	\subsection{Translated spectral growth and physical masks}
    33	
    34	\begin{proposition}[Translated spectral mass]\label{P:masked-spectral-growth}
    35	  Put
    36	  \[
    37	    M_\Gamma = \int_{\R^d}e^{-|x|^2/4}\Gamma(\ud x),
    38	    \qquad C_\Gamma = \frac{eM_\Gamma}{(2\sqrt{\pi})^d}.
    39	  \]
    40	  Then $0 < M_\Gamma < \infty$, and for $y \in \R^d$ and $r > 0$,
    41	  \begin{align}
    42	    \int_{\R^d}e^{-|\xi-y|^2/r^2}\mu(\ud\xi)
    43	    &= \left(\frac{r}{2\sqrt{\pi}}\right)^d
    44	    \int_{\R^d}e^{-r^2|x|^2/4}e^{-iy\cdot x}\Gamma(\ud x),
    45	    \label{E:masked-gaussian-transform}\\
    46	    0 \le \int_{\R^d}e^{-|\xi-y|^2/r^2}\mu(\ud\xi)
    47	    &\le \frac{r^\alpha M_\Gamma}{(2\sqrt{\pi})^d},
    48	    \qquad \mu(B(y,r)) \le C_\Gamma r^\alpha.
    49	    \label{E:masked-translated-ball}
    50	  \end{align}
    51	  The ball may be open or closed.
    52	\end{proposition}
    53	
    54	\begin{proof}
    55	  Temperedness gives finiteness of $M_\Gamma$. Its positivity follows from
    56	  $\Gamma \ne 0$. To check the Fourier constant, set $J(b) = \int_\R
    57	  e^{-Ax^2}e^{ibx}\ud x$ for $A > 0$. Squaring the real Gaussian integral and
    58	  using polar coordinates gives $J(0) = \sqrt{\pi/A}$. Differentiation and
    59	  integration by parts give $J'(b) = -bJ(b)/(2A)$. Therefore, $J(b) =
    60	  \sqrt{\pi/A}e^{-b^2/(4A)}$. Taking products over the coordinates gives
    61	  \[
    62	    \int_{\R^d}e^{-r^2|x|^2/4}e^{i(\xi-y)\cdot x}\ud x
    63	    = \left(\frac{2\sqrt{\pi}}r\right)^d e^{-|\xi-y|^2/r^2}.
    64	  \]
    65	  Apply~\eqref{E:masked-spectral-convention} to the single Schwartz test
    66	  $e^{-r^2|x|^2/4}e^{-iy\cdot x}$ to obtain \eqref{E:masked-gaussian-transform}.
    67	  Its left side is nonnegative. Taking the absolute value on the right removes
    68	  the complex phase because $\Gamma$ is nonnegative. The pushforward of $\Gamma$
    69	  by $x \mapsto rx$ assigns mass $r^{\alpha-d}\Gamma(A)$ to a Borel set $A$.
    70	  Thus,
    71	  \[
    72	    \int e^{-r^2|x|^2/4}\Gamma(\ud x) = r^{\alpha-d}M_\Gamma.
    73	  \]
    74	  This proves the Gaussian bound. On either ball $B(y,r)$ the integrand
    75	  $e^{-|\xi-y|^2/r^2}$ is at least $e^{-1}$, proving the mass bound. This proves
    76	  Proposition~\ref{P:masked-spectral-growth}.
    77	\end{proof}
    78	
    79	Choose and fix a real nonzero Schwartz function $\zeta$. For $R > 0$ put
    80	$\zeta_R(x) = \zeta(x/R)$, $k_R = \widehat{\zeta_R}$ and $L =
    81	\|\widehat{\zeta}\|_1$. Then $k_R(u) = R^d\widehat{\zeta}(Ru)$ and $\|k_R\|_1 =
    82	L > 0$. Define
    83	\begin{equation}\label{E:masked-auxiliary-measure}
    84	  \nu_R(\ud\eta) = \rho_R(\eta)\ud\eta,
    85	  \qquad \rho_R(\eta) = c_d^2L\int |k_R(\xi-\eta)|\mu(\ud\xi).
    86	\end{equation}
    87	
    88	\begin{proposition}[Auxiliary mask norm]\label{P:masked-auxiliary-norm}
    89	  The measure $\nu_R$ is even, tempered and Radon, with
    90	  \begin{equation}\label{E:masked-auxiliary-growth}
    91	    \nu_R(B(y,r)) \le c_d^2L^2C_\Gamma r^\alpha
    92	  \end{equation}

    23	\begin{lemma}[Gaussian envelope for the original covariance]
    24	  \label{L:variational-heat-envelope}
    25	  For the normalized heat kernel $p_\epsilon(x) =
    26	  (2\pi\epsilon)^{-d/2}e^{-|x|^2/(2\epsilon)}$,
    27	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-heat-envelope}
    28	    (\Gamma*p_\epsilon)(x)
    29	    =\int e^{i\xi\cdot x}e^{-\epsilon|\xi|^2/2}\mu(\ud\xi),
    30	    \qquad
    31	    0\le(\Gamma*p_\epsilon)(x)
    32	    \le(\Gamma*p_\epsilon)(0)<\infty.
    33	  \end{equation}
    34	  The value at zero is strictly positive.
    35	\end{lemma}
    36	
    37	\begin{proof}
    38	  A positive tempered Radon measure has polynomial ball growth. Indeed, evaluate
    39	  its tempered bound on a nonnegative smooth cutoff equal to one on $B_1$,
    40	  dilated by $R \ge 1$. Its finitely many Schwartz seminorms are bounded by
    41	  $CR^N$, so positivity gives a ball-mass bound $CR^N$. Summing dyadic annuli
    42	  shows that $(1+|x|)^{-L}$ is integrable for $L > N$. Apply this separately to
    43	  $\Gamma$ and $\mu$. Gaussian weights are therefore integrable against both
    44	  measures. The classical convolution on the left is finite and smooth locally
    45	  in $x$: on compact $x$ sets its translated Gaussian derivatives are bounded by
    46	  any fixed sufficiently fast polynomial weight in the integration variable.
    47	
    48	  Pair the convolution with a Schwartz test $\varphi$. Absolute Fubini is
    49	  justified by these weights. The resulting pairing is that of $\Gamma$ with
    50	  $p_\epsilon*\varphi$. Applying the spectral convention in
    51	  Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog} and the identity $\int p_\epsilon(y)e^{-i\xi\cdot
    52	  y}\ud y = e^{-\epsilon|\xi|^2/2}$ gives exactly the right side
    53	  of~\eqref{E:variational-heat-envelope} as a distribution. The heat kernel is
    54	  even, so either Fourier sign gives that same Gaussian multiplier. Its spectral
    55	  integral is absolutely finite and continuous in $x$ by dominated convergence.
    56	  Thus, equality of the two continuous distributions gives equality at every
    57	  $x$, without an extra normalization factor. The physical convolution is
    58	  nonnegative. Evenness of $\mu$ makes the spectral integral real, and its
    59	  absolute value is bounded by its total Gaussian mass, the value at zero.
    60	  Finally, $\Gamma \ne 0$ and $p_\epsilon > 0$ give strict positivity there.
    61	  This proves Lemma~\ref{L:variational-heat-envelope}.
    62	\end{proof}

   322	    = 2\operatorname{Re}\int_0^h v^{-a}e^{i\omega v}c(v)\ud v
   323	    = 2h^{2-a}\operatorname{Re}\int_0^1 y^{-a}e^{i\omega hy}f(y)\ud y,
   324	  \]
   325	  where $f(y) = c(hy)/h$. Set $K = M+hD$. Then $f(1) = 0$ and $|f|,|f'| \le
   326	  K^2$. If $K = 0$ the assertion is immediate. If $|\omega h| \le 1$, the last
   327	  integral is at most $K^2/(1-a)$ in absolute value, and $\langle\omega
   328	  h\rangle^{a-1} \ge 2^{(a-1)/2}$. The claimed constant is sufficient in this
   329	  case.
   330	
   331	  Now suppose $k = |\omega h| > 1$. On $[0,1/k]$ the integral is at most
   332	  $K^2k^{a-1}/(1-a)$. On $[1/k,1]$, integrate the exponential by parts. The
   333	  endpoint at one vanishes, while the other endpoint contributes at most
   334	  $K^2k^{a-1}$. The derivative integral, divided by $k$, is bounded by
   335	  \[
   336	    \frac{K^2}k\left(a\int_{1/k}^1 y^{-a-1}\ud y
   337	    +\int_{1/k}^1 y^{-a}\ud y\right)
   338	    \le K^2 k^{a-1}\left(1+\frac1{1-a}\right).
   339	  \]
   340	  Here $k^{-1} \le k^{a-1}$ since $a > 0$. The total is at most
   341	  $4K^2k^{a-1}/(1-a)$. Finally, $k^{a-1} \le \sqrt{2}\langle\omega
   342	  h\rangle^{a-1}$ and $8\sqrt{2} \le 16$. Including the factor $2h^{2-a}$ proves
   343	  the bound for either sign of $\omega$. This proves
   344	  Lemma~\ref{L:masked-temporal-modulation}.
   345	\end{proof}

   347	\begin{lemma}[Correlated trigonometric products]\label{L:masked-trig-products}
   348	  Let $r,\rho \ge 0$. Let $P_r$ be either $\cos(rt)$ or $\sin(rt)$, and let
   349	  $Q_\rho$ be either $\cos(\rho t)$ or $\sin(\rho t)$. With the amplitude and
   350	  constant above,
   351	  \begin{align}
   352	    \|1_IAP_rQ_\rho\|_a^2
   353	    &\le C_0(a)h^{2-a}(M+hD)^2\mathcal{Q}_h(r,\rho),
   354	    \label{E:masked-trig-products}\\
   355	    \mathcal{Q}_h(r,\rho)
   356	    &:= \langle h(r-\rho)\rangle^{a-1}
   357	    +\langle h(r+\rho)\rangle^{a-1}.
   358	    \label{E:masked-frequency-pair}
   359	  \end{align}
   360	\end{lemma}
   361	
   362	\begin{proof}
   363	  Expanding the two trigonometric factors gives four complex exponential modes
   364	  with frequencies $\sigma r+\tau\rho$, $\sigma,\tau \in \{-1,1\}$, and
   365	  coefficients of absolute value $1/4$. In a Hilbert space,
   366	  \[
   367	    \left\|\sum_j c_jv_j\right\|^2
   368	    \le \left(\sum_j|c_j|\right)\sum_j|c_j|\|v_j\|^2.
   369	  \]
   370	  The first coefficient sum is one. Apply
   371	  Lemma~\ref{L:masked-temporal-modulation} to each mode. Two frequencies have
   372	  absolute value $|r-\rho|$ and two have absolute value $r+\rho$. This gives one
   373	  half of the asserted right side, and hence the bound. Repeated or zero
   374	  frequencies are permitted; no orthogonality or independence of the modes is
   375	  used. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:masked-trig-products}.
   376	\end{proof}

   378	\begin{lemma}[Continuous sine factors]\label{L:masked-continuous-wave}
   379	  Define $c_r(t) = \cos(rt)$ and
   380	  \[
   381	    b_r(t) = \langle r\rangle\frac{\sin(rt)}r\quad(r > 0),
   382	    \qquad b_0(t) = t.
   383	  \]
   384	  For $F_r \in \{c_r,b_r\}$ and $G_\rho \in \{c_\rho,b_\rho\}$,
   385	  \begin{equation}\label{E:masked-continuous-wave}
   386	    \|1_IF_rG_\rho\|_a^2
   387	    \le C_1(a)(1+T)^4h^{2-a}\mathcal{Q}_h(r,\rho),
   388	    \qquad C_1(a) = 4\cdot3^{1-a}C_0(a).
   389	  \end{equation}
   390	\end{lemma}
   391	
   392	\begin{proof}
   393	  For $r \ge 1$, $b_r$ is a sine times a coefficient at most $\sqrt{2}$. For $0
   394	  \le r \le 1$, the fundamental theorem of calculus gives
   395	  \[
   396	    b_r(t) = t\langle r\rangle\int_0^1\cos(vrt)\ud v.
   397	  \]
   398	  This includes $r = 0$. Hence, a product $F_rG_\rho$ is a scalar coefficient of
   399	  absolute value at most two times a normalized integral of
   400	  $t^jP_{r'}(t)Q_{\rho'}(t)$, where $j \in \{0,1,2\}$ and $|r'-r|,|\rho'-\rho|
   401	  \le 1$. The integral is over zero, one or two copies of $[0,1]$; with no
   402	  averages, use a one-point probability space. Its parameter dependence is
   403	  continuous in $L^2(0,T)$ by dominated convergence.
   404	  Lemma~\ref{L:masked-time-completion} makes it continuous in $H_a$ as well.
   405	  Thus, the averages are Bochner integrals, and their $H_a$ images agree with
   406	  the pointwise averages by continuity of the inclusion. Hilbert Jensen bounds
   407	  the squared norm of an average by the average of the squared norms.
   408	
   409	  Apply Lemma~\ref{L:masked-trig-products} to each integrand with $A(t) = t^j$.
   410	  For $j = 0,1,2$, respectively, $M+hD$ is at most $1$, $T+1$ and $T^2+2T$. In
   411	  every case $(M+hD)^2 \le (1+T)^4$. For real $x,e$, the triangle inequality and
   412	  its reverse imply
   413	  \[
   414	    \frac{\langle x\rangle}{1+|e|}
   415	    \le \langle x+e\rangle \le (1+|e|)\langle x\rangle.
   416	  \]
   417	  The changes in $h(r\pm\rho)$ have magnitude at most two, since $h \le 1$.
   418	  Because $a-1 < 0$, each altered bracket to the power $a-1$ is at most
   419	  $3^{1-a}$ times the original one. Apply these comparisons, Hilbert Jensen and
   420	  the squared scalar coefficient bound four to obtain
   421	  \eqref{E:masked-continuous-wave}. This proves
   422	  Lemma~\ref{L:masked-continuous-wave}.
   423	\end{proof}

    13	  B_\alpha(h) =
    14	  \begin{cases}
    15	    1, & \alpha < 1,\\
    16	    1+\log(1/h), & \alpha = 1,\\

    22	\subsection{A scalar row estimate for a measure}
    23	
    24	Let $\nu$ be a positive Radon measure satisfying
    25	\begin{equation}\label{E:frequency-translated-growth}
    26	  \nu(B(y,r)) \le C r^\alpha,
    27	  \qquad y \in \R^d,\quad r > 0,
    28	\end{equation}
    29	where $C \ge 0$. If the estimate is initially known for open balls, apply it at
    30	radius $r+\epsilon$ and let $\epsilon \downarrow 0$ to obtain the closed-ball
    31	estimate. Neither evenness nor a density is assumed here.
    32	Using~\eqref{E:masked-frequency-pair}, define
    33	\begin{align}
    34	  \Phi_h(\xi,\eta)
    35	  &:= \frac{\mathcal{Q}_h(|\xi|,|\eta|)}
    36	  {\langle\xi\rangle\langle\eta\rangle},
    37	  \label{E:frequency-row-kernel}\\
    38	  J_h(\xi)
    39	  &:= \langle\xi\rangle^{2\gamma}
    40	  \int_{\R^d}\Phi_h(\xi,\xi-\lambda)\nu(\ud\lambda).
    41	  \label{E:frequency-row-integral}
    42	\end{align}
    43	These are initially nonnegative extended integrals. In particular, the notation
    44	denotes a pushforward of $\nu$, not integration against an assumed spectral
    45	density.
    46	
    47	\begin{proposition}[Uniform scalar row]\label{P:frequency-row}
    48	  There is a finite $K = K(\alpha,a,\gamma)$, independent of $d,\nu,C,h$ and
    49	  $\xi$, such that
    50	  \begin{equation}\label{E:frequency-row-bound}
    51	    \sup_{\xi\in\R^d}J_h(\xi) \le K C B_\alpha(h),
    52	    \qquad 0 < h \le 1.
    53	  \end{equation}
    54	\end{proposition}
    55	
    56	\begin{proof}
    57	  If $C = 0$, a countable covering by finite balls gives $\nu = 0$, and the
    58	  result is immediate. Suppose $C > 0$. For each $\xi$, let $\nu_\xi$ be the
    59	  pushforward under $\lambda \mapsto \eta = \xi-\lambda$. Then $\nu_\xi(B(0,R))
    60	  \le CR^\alpha$. For $q \ge 1$, put
    61	  \[
    62	    A_\xi(q) = \int_{|\eta|\le5q}\langle\eta\rangle^{-1}
    63	    \nu_\xi(\ud\eta).
    64	  \]
    65	  Choose $N = \lceil\log_2(5q)\rceil$, so $5q \le 2^N < 10q$. Splitting into the
    66	  unit ball and the annuli $2^j < |\eta| \le 2^{j+1}$ gives
    67	  \[
    68	    A_\xi(q) \le C\left(1+2^\alpha
    69	    \sum_{j=0}^{N-1}2^{j(\alpha-1)}\right).
    70	  \]
    71	  The geometric sum is bounded when $\alpha < 1$, is $N$ when $\alpha = 1$, and
    72	  is at most $2^{N(\alpha-1)}/(2^{\alpha-1}-1)$ when $\alpha > 1$. Hence,
    73	  \begin{equation}\label{E:frequency-inverse-bessel}
    74	    A_\xi(q) \le K_\alpha C
    75	    \begin{cases}
    76	      1, & \alpha < 1,\\
    77	      1+\log q, & \alpha = 1,\\
    78	      q^{\alpha-1}, & \alpha > 1,
    79	    \end{cases}
    80	  \end{equation}
    81	  with a constant depending only on $\alpha$.
    82	
    83	  Set $q = \max(1,|\xi|)$ and $\epsilon = 1-2\gamma > 0$. On $|\lambda| \le 4q$
    84	  we have $|\eta| \le 5q$. Both bracket powers in $\mathcal{Q}_h$ are at most
    85	  one, since $a-1 < 0$. The contribution of this region to $J_h(\xi)$ is at most
    86	  \[
    87	    2\langle\xi\rangle^{-\epsilon}A_\xi(q)
    88	    \le 2q^{-\epsilon}A_\xi(q).
    89	  \]
    90	  If $\alpha < 1$, this is uniformly bounded
    91	  by~\eqref{E:frequency-inverse-bessel}. If $\alpha = 1$, the bound follows from
    92	  \[
    93	    e^{-\epsilon u}(1+u) \le 1+\frac1{e\epsilon},
    94	    \qquad u = \log q \ge 0,
    95	  \]
    96	  since $u e^{-\epsilon u}$ has maximum $1/(e\epsilon)$. If $\alpha > 1$, the
    97	  remaining power is $q^{\alpha+2\gamma-2}$, whose exponent is negative
    98	  by~\eqref{E:variance-gamma-range}. Thus, the near contribution is at most a
    99	  constant times $C$ in all three cases.
   100	
   101	  On the far region write $r = |\lambda| > 4q$. Then
   102	  \[
   103	    |\eta| \ge \frac{3r}4,\qquad
   104	    \big||\eta|-|\xi|\big| \ge \frac r2,\qquad
   105	    |\eta|+|\xi| \ge \frac r2.
   106	  \]
   107	  Each oscillatory bracket is at least $\langle hr\rangle/2$, whereas
   108	  $\langle\eta\rangle^{-1} \le 4/(3r)$ and $\langle\xi\rangle^{-\epsilon} \le
   109	  1$. Consequently, the far contribution is at most
   110	  \[
   111	    \frac43\,2^{2-a}\int_{|\lambda|>4q}
   112	    |\lambda|^{-1}\langle h|\lambda|\rangle^{a-1}\nu(\ud\lambda).
   113	  \]
   114	  Enlarge the domain to $|\lambda| > 1$ and split it into dyadic annuli.
   115	  Applying~\eqref{E:frequency-translated-growth} to their masses bounds this
   116	  expression by a constant depending only on $\alpha,a$ times $C S(h)$, where
   117	  \[
   118	    S(h) = \sum_{j=0}^\infty
   119	    2^{j(\alpha-1)}\langle h2^j\rangle^{a-1}.
   120	  \]
   121	  Choose $L = \lfloor\log_2(1/h)\rfloor \ge 0$. For $j \le L$ the bracket power
   122	  is at most one. For $j \ge L+1$ it is at most $(h2^j)^{a-1}$. Since
   123	  $\alpha+a-2 < 0$, the tail is
   124	  \[
   125	    \frac{h^{a-1}2^{(L+1)(\alpha+a-2)}}{1-2^{\alpha+a-2}}
   126	    \le \frac{h^{1-\alpha}}{1-2^{\alpha+a-2}}.
   127	  \]
   128	  The inequality uses $2^{L+1} > 1/h$ and the negative exponent. The finite sum
   129	  is bounded by $1/(1-2^{\alpha-1})$ for $\alpha < 1$, by $1+\log_2(1/h)$ for
   130	  $\alpha = 1$, and by
   131	  \[
   132	    \frac{2^{\alpha-1}h^{1-\alpha}}{2^{\alpha-1}-1}
   133	  \]
   134	  for $\alpha > 1$. Since $h^{1-\alpha} \le 1$ in the first case, we obtain
   135	  $S(h) \le K_{\alpha,a}B_\alpha(h)$. Combining the near and far bounds, and
   136	  using $B_\alpha(h) \ge 1$, proves the assertion and finiteness of the original
   137	  integral. All constants arose from numerical shell estimates and are
   138	  independent of $d$. This proves Proposition~\ref{P:frequency-row}.
   139	\end{proof}

   141	\begin{corollary}[A time exponent above one half]\label{C:frequency-time}
   142	  For every
   143	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variance-beta-range}
   144	    \frac12 < \beta < \min\left(1-\frac a2,
   145	    \frac{3-a-\alpha}{2}\right),
   146	  \end{equation}
   147	  there is a finite $K_\beta = K_\beta(\alpha,a,\gamma,\beta)$ such that
   148	  \begin{equation}\label{E:frequency-time-bound}
   149	    h^{2-a}\sup_\xi J_h(\xi) \le K_\beta C h^{2\beta},
   150	    \qquad 0 < h \le 1.
   151	  \end{equation}
   152	\end{corollary}
   153	
   154	\begin{proof}
   155	  Both upper endpoints in~\eqref{E:variance-beta-range} exceed one half, by $a <
   156	  1$ and $\alpha+a < 2$. If $\alpha < 1$, use $2-a > 2\beta$ in
   157	  Proposition~\ref{P:frequency-row}. If $\alpha > 1$, use $3-a-\alpha > 2\beta$.
   158	  For $\alpha = 1$, set $\delta = 2-a-2\beta > 0$ and $u = \log(1/h)$. Then
   159	  \[
   160	    h^\delta(1+\log(1/h))
   161	    = e^{-\delta u}(1+u) \le 1+\frac1{e\delta}.
   162	  \]
   163	  This absorbs the critical logarithm. No endpoint value of $\beta$ is used.
   164	  This proves Corollary~\ref{C:frequency-time}.
   165	\end{proof}

   167	\subsection{Forms on the full phase}
   168	
   169	Choose and fix $T > 0$. Set $\Lambda = (1-\Delta)^{1/2}$, $s = 1/2$ and $E_r =
   170	H^r(\R^d)\times H^{r-1}(\R^d)$. On the complexification of $E = E_s$, use inner

   173	  Jz(\xi) = \left(\langle\xi\rangle^{1/2}\widehat{z}_1(\xi),

   177	Fourier matrix
   178	\begin{equation}\label{E:variance-free-matrix}
   179	  S(t,\xi) =
   180	  \begin{pmatrix}
   181	    \cos(t|\xi|) & \sin(t|\xi|)/|\xi|\\

   212	\begin{proposition}[Form and phase kernel]\label{P:actual-wave-form}
   213	  The tests $\zeta_RF_{z,w}$ in~\eqref{E:variance-actual-form} belong to the
   214	  original noise completion. The form $\ell_R$ is linear in $z$ and conjugate
   215	  linear in $w$, and uses the same $W$ as the model. For a smooth deterministic
   216	  coefficient $b$ with common compact spatial support and bounded spatial
   217	  derivatives on $[0,T]$,
   218	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variance-physical-adjoint}
   219	    \langle S(-t)B(b(t))S(t)z,w\rangle_E
   220	    = \int b(t,x)v_z(t,x)\overline{G_w(t,x)}\ud x.
   221	  \end{equation}
   222	  For a real compact smooth $\chi$, multiplication $D_\chi$ on both phase
   223	  entries has adjoint
   224	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variance-cutoff-adjoint}
   225	    D_\chi^{*,E}w
   226	    = \left(\Lambda^{-1}\chi\Lambda w_1,
   227	    \Lambda\chi\Lambda^{-1}w_2\right).

   229	  With $U = Jz$, $V = Jw$, $r = |\xi|$, $\rho = |\eta|$ and the continuous
   230	  functions $c_r,b_r$ of Lemma~\ref{L:masked-continuous-wave}, set
   231	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variance-normalized-kernel}
   232	    \mathcal{K}(t;\xi,\eta)
   233	    = \frac1{\sqrt{\langle\xi\rangle\langle\eta\rangle}}
   234	    \begin{pmatrix}
   235	      -b_rc_\rho & -b_rb_\rho\\
   236	      c_rc_\rho & c_rb_\rho
   237	    \end{pmatrix}(t).
   238	  \end{equation}

   240	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variance-normalized-covariance}
   241	    \E|\ell_R(I;z,w)|^2
   242	    \le \int\left\|\int\sum_{i,j=1}^2
   243	    1_I\mathcal{K}_{ij}(\cdot;\eta+\lambda,\eta)
   244	    U_j(\eta)\overline{V_i(\eta+\lambda)}\ud\eta
   245	    \right\|_{H_a^{\mathbb{C}}}^2\nu_R(\ud\lambda).

   248	
   249	\begin{proof}
   250	  The wave multipliers are smooth at zero through the continuous sine quotient,
   251	  with polynomially bounded frequency derivatives on finite time intervals.
   252	  Bessel multipliers preserve Schwartz space. Thus, $v_z,G_w$ and their product
   253	  are continuous in all Schwartz seminorms on $[0,T]$. For tests supported in a
   254	  fixed compact $K$, the absolute spatial pairing is bounded by
   255	  \[
   256	    |K|\Gamma(K-K)\|F(t)\|_\infty\|H(u)\|_\infty.
   257	  \]

   259	  F(t,x)\overline{H(u,x-y)}\ud x$. Combine this with the temporal Schur bound
   260	  and approximate the interval indicator and the continuous time dependence by
   261	  smooth interior temporal tests, keeping the spatial support of $\zeta_R$. This
   262	  admits the masked product in the original completion in every allowed
   263	  dimension.
   264	
   265	  We also identify its auxiliary and spectral limits. Approximate a
   266	  Schwartz-valued function on $I$ by time partitions with frozen spatial values,
   267	  and then replace the finitely many indicators by compact smooth temporal
   268	  functions. A diagonal sequence $F_n$ of finite temporal tensors converges in
   269	  $L^2$ time in every Schwartz seminorm. Fourier integration by parts and the
   270	  spatial weighted supremum bounds give, for sufficiently large fixed $N$,
   271	  \[
   272	    \|\widehat{F_n-F}(\xi)\|_{L^2(0,T)}
   273	    \le \epsilon_n\langle\xi\rangle^{-N},\qquad \epsilon_n \to 0.
   274	  \]
   275	  Choose $N$ so that the square weight is integrable against both tempered
   276	  measures $\mu$ and $\nu_R$. Lemma~\ref{L:masked-time-completion} gives
   277	  convergence in their spectral $H_a$ norms. Multiplication by the fixed
   278	  $\zeta_R$ preserves these $L^2$ Schwartz-seminorm limits, so the masked
   279	  differences converge in the $\mu$ spectral norm too. The preceding
   280	  compact-support estimate also gives convergence in the original completion.
   281	  Hence, the auxiliary extension and original-noise limit agree on these
   282	  products. Constants for this admission argument may depend on $R$; they are
   283	  not the uniform variance constants below.
   284	
   285	  For real tensor tests $f,g$, the Hermitian symmetry of their spatial
   286	  transforms gives
   287	  \[
   288	    A(-\xi) = \overline{A(\xi)},\qquad
   289	    A(\xi) = \langle\widehat{f}(\xi),\widehat{g}(\xi)\rangle_{H_a^{\mathbb{C}}}.
   290	  \]
   291	  Integration against either even $\mu$ or even $\nu_R$ cancels the imaginary
   292	  mixed term. Expanding the squared norm of $\widehat{f}+i\widehat{g}$, then
   293	  using the preceding approximation, extends
   294	  Proposition~\ref{P:masked-noise-completion} to the present complex tests:
   295	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variance-complex-noise}
   296	    \E|W_{\mathbb{C}}(\zeta_RF)|^2
   297	    = (2\pi)^d\int\|\widehat{\zeta_RF}(\xi)\|_{H_a^{\mathbb{C}}}^2\mu(\ud\xi)
   298	    \le (2\pi)^d\int\|\widehat{F}(\lambda)\|_{H_a^{\mathbb{C}}}^2\nu_R(\ud\lambda).
   299	  \end{equation}
   300	  This is a bound for the masked noise, not a declaration that its law is
   301	  stationary. Complex linearity of $W_{\mathbb{C}}$ and linearity of $v_z,G_w$
   302	  prove the stated sesquilinearity.
   303	
   304	  Smooth multiplication is bounded on each Sobolev space: Fourier convolution,
   305	  the inequality $\langle\xi\rangle^r\langle\eta\rangle^{-r} \le
   306	  2^{|r|/2}\langle\xi-\eta\rangle^{|r|}$ and weighted Schwartz decay reduce this
   307	  to the $L^1*L^2$ bound. The free matrix is strongly continuous and bounded on
   308	  $E$ on compact time intervals, directly by its weighted Fourier entries. Thus,
   309	  the ordinary first-response integral exists on states. Since $S(-t)(0,f) =
   310	  (-\sin(t|D|)f/|D|,\cos(t|D|)f)$, moving the real self-adjoint multipliers and
   311	  the two Sobolev weights onto $w$ proves \eqref{E:variance-physical-adjoint}.
   312	  The same weighted duality gives \eqref{E:variance-cutoff-adjoint}. Inserting
   313	  this adjoint in $G_w$ is the correctly observed form; $D_\chi$ need not be
   314	  self-adjoint on $E$. This deterministic identity does not identify a
   315	  positive-width source with the original noise or assert a source limit.

   317	  The definitions give exactly
   318	  \begin{align*}
   319	    \widehat{v}_z(t,\eta)
   320	    &= \langle\eta\rangle^{-1/2}
   321	    [c_\rho(t)U_1(\eta)+b_\rho(t)U_2(\eta)],\\
   322	    \widehat{G}_w(t,\xi)
   323	    &= \langle\xi\rangle^{-1/2}
   324	    [-b_r(t)V_1(\xi)+c_r(t)V_2(\xi)].
   325	  \end{align*}

   327	  one uses the continuous sine quotient, not division by zero; at $\xi = \eta =
   328	  0$ the matrix is
   329	  $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}-t&-t^2\\1&t\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. Fourier
   330	  multiplication with the conjugate yields
   331	  \[
   332	    \widehat{F}_{z,w}(t,-\lambda)
   333	    = c_d1_I(t)\int\sum_{i,j=1}^2\mathcal{K}_{ij}(t;\eta+\lambda,\eta)
   334	    U_j(\eta)\overline{V_i(\eta+\lambda)}\ud\eta.
   335	  \]

   337	  interval by Schwartz decay. The Schur bound also makes it a Bochner
   338	  $H_a^{\mathbb{C}}$ integral. Reflect $\lambda$ using evenness of $\nu_R$
   339	  in~\eqref{E:variance-complex-noise}. Since $(2\pi)^dc_d^2 = 1$, this
   340	  proves~\eqref{E:variance-normalized-covariance} with no remaining Fourier
   341	  factor. This proves Proposition~\ref{P:actual-wave-form}.

   344	\subsection{Bessel's inequality and the two variances}
   345	
   346	\begin{lemma}[Hilbert-valued finite Bessel inequality]\label{L:phase-bessel}
   347	  Let $H$ be a separable complex Hilbert space, let $\{u_k\}$ be a finite
   348	  orthonormal family in $L^2(\R^d;\mathbb{C}^2)$, and let $g = (g_1,g_2) \in
   349	  L^2(\R^d;H^2)$. Then
   350	  \begin{equation}\label{E:phase-bessel}
   351	    \sum_k\left\|\int\sum_{j=1}^2u_{k,j}(\eta)g_j(\eta)\ud\eta\right\|_H^2
   352	    \le \int\sum_{j=1}^2\|g_j(\eta)\|_H^2\ud\eta.
   353	  \end{equation}
   354	  The same bound holds with $\overline{u_{k,j}}$ in place of $u_{k,j}$.
   355	\end{lemma}
   356	
   357	\begin{proof}
   358	  Expand $g$ in a countable orthonormal basis of $H$. On each scalar coefficient
   359	  apply scalar Bessel to the orthonormal family $\{\overline{u_k}\}$, or to
   360	  $\{u_k\}$ for the conjugated version. Scalar finite Bessel follows by
   361	  subtracting an orthogonal finite projection and expanding its nonnegative
   362	  squared norm. Sum over the $H$ basis and use Parseval and nonnegative Tonelli.
   363	  The Bochner integrals exist by $L^2$ Cauchy--Schwarz. A finite-dimensional $H$
   364	  uses its finite basis, and the zero space is immediate. No independence is
   365	  involved. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:phase-bessel}.
   366	\end{proof}
   367	
   368	\begin{proposition}[Both variance directions]\label{P:wave-two-variances}
   369	  There is a finite $C_T$, depending on the fixed model, mask,
   370	  $a,\alpha,\gamma,T$, but not on $R,I$ or the orthonormal family, such that for
   371	  every finite complex $E$-orthonormal Schwartz family $\{e_k\}$ and every
   372	  Schwartz phase $z$,
   373	  \begin{align}
   374	    \sum_k\E|\ell_R(I;e_k,z)|^2
   375	    &\le C_T h^{2-a}B_\alpha(h)\|z\|_{E_{s-\gamma}}^2,
   376	    \label{E:wave-input-variance}\\
   377	    \sum_k\E|\ell_R(I;z,e_k)|^2
   378	    &\le C_T h^{2-a}B_\alpha(h)\|z\|_{E_{s-\gamma}}^2.
   379	    \label{E:wave-output-variance}
   380	  \end{align}
   381	  For every $\beta$ in~\eqref{E:variance-beta-range}, either right side may be
   382	  replaced by $C_{T,\beta}h^{2\beta}\|z\|_{E_{s-\gamma}}^2$.
   383	\end{proposition}
   384	
   385	\begin{proof}
   386	  Each entry in~\eqref{E:variance-normalized-kernel} is a product of two
   387	  continuous wave factors times $(\langle\xi\rangle\langle\eta\rangle)^{-1/2}$,
   388	  with a possible minus sign. Lemma~\ref{L:masked-continuous-wave} therefore
   389	  gives
   390	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variance-kernel-time-bound}
   391	    \|1_I\mathcal{K}_{ij}(\cdot;\xi,\eta)\|_{H_a^{\mathbb{C}}}^2
   392	    \le A_T h^{2-a}\Phi_h(\xi,\eta),
   393	    \qquad A_T = C_1(a)(1+T)^4.
   394	  \end{equation}
   395	  The positive even Radon measure $\nu_R$ satisfies the growth bound
   396	  \eqref{E:variance-actual-growth-constant}. Thus, all hypotheses of
   397	  Proposition~\ref{P:frequency-row} hold, and
   398	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variance-actual-row-bound}
   399	    \int\Phi_h(\xi,\xi-\lambda)\nu_R(\ud\lambda)
   400	    \le K C_\nu B_\alpha(h)\langle\xi\rangle^{-2\gamma}.
   401	  \end{equation}
   402	  No nonnegative physical inverse covariance of $\nu_R$ is needed.
   403	
   404	  The kernels used in Lemma~\ref{L:phase-bessel} belong to its stated $L^2$
   405	  space for each fixed $\lambda$. Indeed, $|c_r(t)| \le 1$ and $|b_r(t)| \le
   406	  \sqrt{2}\max(1,T)$ on $[0,T]$, by the high- and low-frequency representations.
   407	  The kernels are continuous into $L^2(0,T)$ in their frequency variables, hence
   408	  into $H_a^{\mathbb{C}}$ by Schur. Separability gives strong measurability.
   409	  Multiplication by shifted Schwartz components of $U$ or $V$ then gives the
   410	  required $L^2$ integrability. Later $\lambda$ integrals are of nonnegative
   411	  functions; their finiteness follows from the estimates below.
   412	
   413	  First fix $V = Jz$ and let $U_k = Je_k$ be the input family.
   414	  In~\eqref{E:variance-normalized-covariance} set
   415	  \[
   416	    g_j^\lambda(\eta) = \sum_{i=1}^2
   417	    1_I\mathcal{K}_{ij}(\cdot;\eta+\lambda,\eta)
   418	    \overline{V_i(\eta+\lambda)}.
   419	  \]
   420	  Lemma~\ref{L:phase-bessel} and Cauchy--Schwarz over the two output components
   421	  give
   422	  \begin{align*}
   423	    \sum_j\|g_j^\lambda(\eta)\|_{H_a^{\mathbb{C}}}^2
   424	    &\le 2\sum_{i,j}|V_i(\eta+\lambda)|^2
   425	    \|1_I\mathcal{K}_{ij}(\cdot;\eta+\lambda,\eta)\|_{H_a^{\mathbb{C}}}^2\\
   426	    &\le 4A_T h^{2-a}\Phi_h(\eta+\lambda,\eta)
   427	    \sum_i|V_i(\eta+\lambda)|^2.
   428	  \end{align*}
   429	  Change variables $\xi = \eta+\lambda$ in the Lebesgue integral for each
   430	  $\lambda$, apply Tonelli and~\eqref{E:variance-actual-row-bound}, and use
   431	  $\|z\|_{E_{s-\gamma}} = \|\langle\xi\rangle^{-\gamma}Jz\|_2$. This
   432	  proves~\eqref{E:wave-input-variance} with $C_T = 4A_TKC_\nu$.
   433	
   434	  Next fix $U = Jz$ and let $V_k = Je_k$ be the output family. After $\eta =
   435	  \xi-\lambda$ in~\eqref{E:variance-normalized-covariance}, put
   436	  \[
   437	    f_i^\lambda(\xi) = \sum_{j=1}^2
   438	    1_I\mathcal{K}_{ij}(\cdot;\xi,\xi-\lambda)U_j(\xi-\lambda).
   439	  \]
   440	  Apply the conjugated version of Lemma~\ref{L:phase-bessel}. Cauchy--Schwarz
   441	  over the two input components bounds its right side by
   442	  \[
   443	    4A_T h^{2-a}\int\Phi_h(\xi,\xi-\lambda)
   444	    \sum_j|U_j(\xi-\lambda)|^2\ud\xi.
   445	  \]
   446	  After the change of variables and Tonelli, the row at fixed $\eta$ is
   447	  $\int\Phi_h(\eta+\lambda,\eta)\nu_R(\ud\lambda)$. Reflect $\lambda$ using the
   448	  evenness of $\nu_R$ and then use symmetry of $\Phi_h$. This row becomes
   449	  $\int\Phi_h(\eta,\eta-\lambda)\nu_R(\ud\lambda)$, which is bounded
   450	  by~\eqref{E:variance-actual-row-bound} with $\xi = \eta$. This proves
   451	  \eqref{E:wave-output-variance} with the same $C_T$.
   452	
   453	  Use Corollary~\ref{C:frequency-time} for $h^{2-a}$ times the row integral at
   454	  the two applications above to obtain the asserted $h^{2\beta}$ bounds,
   455	  including strict absorption of the critical logarithm. The constants are
   456	  uniform in $R,I$ and family size. The $R$-dependent admission estimate was not
   457	  used as this uniform variance bound. This proves
   458	  Proposition~\ref{P:wave-two-variances}.
   459	\end{proof}

   270	\begin{proposition}[Intrinsic variational lower bounds]
   271	  \label{P:variational-positive-scores}
   272	  For $c > 0$, the set of variational values
   273	  $\{cI_\Psi-v_\Psi/2:\Psi\in\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{pos}}\}$ is nonempty and
   274	  bounded above. Its finite real supremum $S_c^{\mathrm{pos}}$ is positive and
   275	  satisfies
   276	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-score-homogeneity}
   277	    S_c^{\mathrm{pos}}=c^{(4-\alpha)/(3-\alpha)}S_1^{\mathrm{pos}},
   278	    \qquad
   279	    Q_2\ge S_2^{\mathrm{pos}},
   280	  \end{equation}
   281	  where $Q_2$ is the original point liminf. The coefficient-one value is an
   282	  auxiliary variational value; no first-moment or source-constant identification
   283	  is asserted.
   284	\end{proposition}
   285	
   286	\begin{proof}
   287	  Write $k = 3-\alpha > 0$, $q = 4-\alpha = k+1$ and $m = q/k > 1$. Fix one
   288	  $\Psi_0$ from the nonempty class and put $I_0 = I_{\Psi_0} > 0$, $v_0 =
   289	  v_{\Psi_0} > 0$. Positivity of the latter is
   290	  Lemma~\ref{L:compact-raw-profile}. For $r_0 = (I_0/v_0)^{1/k} > 0$, which need
   291	  not be less than one, the exact real-power identity gives
   292	  \[
   293	    I_{D_{r_0}\Psi_0}-v_{D_{r_0}\Psi_0}/2
   294	    =r_0I_0-r_0^qv_0/2=r_0I_0/2>0.
   295	  \]
   296	  This positive value is obtained from a smooth nonnegative control.
   297	
   298	  For $c > 0$ put $r_c = c^{1/k}$ and $K_c = c^m > 0$.
   299	  Lemma~\ref{L:variational-control-dilation} and the exact scalar powers give,
   300	  for every $\Psi$,
   301	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-score-set-scaling}
   302	    cI_{D_{r_c}\Psi}-v_{D_{r_c}\Psi}/2
   303	    =K_c(I_\Psi-v_\Psi/2).
   304	  \end{equation}
   305	  Since $D_{r_c}$ is a bijection of the entire class, the whole set of
   306	  variational values with coefficient $c$ is $K_c$ times the whole
   307	  coefficient-one set of variational values.
   308	
   309	  We prove boundedness before taking finite-real suprema. The independent
   310	  Theorem~\ref{T:full-upper}, for the \emph{same canonical solution}, gives
   311	  \[
   312	    \E|u(T,0)|^2\le e(T+2)^d e^{C_{\mathrm{up}}T^\kappa},
   313	    \qquad T\ge1,\quad C_{\mathrm{up}}<\infty.
   314	  \]
   315	  Its prefactor is negligible: choose $\epsilon = \kappa/2 > 0$, use $\log T \le
   316	  (T^\epsilon-1)/\epsilon$ and $\log(T+2) \le \log T+\log3$ for $T \ge 1$, and
   317	  divide by $T^\kappa$. Thus, the original point limsup is at most
   318	  $C_{\mathrm{up}}$. One fixed test/mask lower bound gives a finite lower bound
   319	  for $Q_2$, so $Q_2$ is finite. By~\eqref{E:variational-unmasked-point-lower}
   320	  every coefficient-two variational expression is at most this same $Q_2 \le
   321	  C_{\mathrm{up}}$, uniformly in $\Psi$.
   322	  Equation~\eqref{E:variational-score-set-scaling} at $c = 2$ consequently
   323	  bounds all coefficient-one variational values by $C_{\mathrm{up}}/K_2$. The
   324	  nonempty set has a finite real supremum $S_1^{\mathrm{pos}} > 0$ by the
   325	  positive test above.
   326	
   327	  For general $c$, set equality and $K_c > 0$ show that $K_cS_1^{\mathrm{pos}}$
   328	  is the supremum: it is an upper bound, and every smaller number is exceeded by
   329	  $K_c$ times a coefficient-one variational expression within the corresponding
   330	  positive distance of its supremum. This proves finiteness, positivity and the
   331	  first identity in~\eqref{E:variational-score-homogeneity}. Taking the
   332	  numerical supremum of the coefficient-two lower bounds proves the second.
   333	  Although $2^m > 2$, the resulting $S_2^{\mathrm{pos}} > 2S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}$
   334	  is only a comparison of auxiliary variational values. It is not a Jensen
   335	  improvement without a first-moment identification. This proves
   336	  Proposition~\ref{P:variational-positive-scores}.
   337	\end{proof}

   368	  \end{equation}

   372	  Dropping the positive quadratic damping bounds the mixture by the Gamma
   373	  integral $|u|^{-a}$. Positivity and monotonicity follow directly from the
   374	  integrand, and $a < 1$ gives local integrability. Put $\Phi(t) =

   377	  equality at $s = 1/2$. The diagonal value changes no time integral. This
   378	  proves Lemma~\ref{L:occupation-kernel-row}.
